text: For the values CG-B2-P7-023-1 leaves open, this story applies these readings: the decision code of a transfer record is taken from LOV-DECISION at run time and its value is not invented; the MSG-P7-009 text, the REQ-CWC-010 text and the rwb-decision login name keep the R9 placeholder; DecisionLogEntry is the TSD P7 v2 T3.1 field set and DecisionLogPage is one page of it with page, size and total; the version list answers a date with no TRANSFER version in force with the finding and MSG-P3-027 naming the package code and the date, never a default; the page size is a service configuration guard with no business value; and a refused record is quarantined on rwb-decision.dlt with an incident that names the case ID and the missing field only.
why: The story must be buildable and testable before the API specification adds the missing detail, and no business value may be invented.
read: Legacy section 12 and section 14; FSD P7 v3 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.7; TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2; Template and Rules v1 R9
confirm: P7 business analyst and solution architect at the wave 2 API specification walkthrough, before the Service Contract Catalog freeze
impact: If a code or a shape differs, only the validator, the DTOs, the reference-data value and the message table change; no version, no rule ID and no check changes

text: The DP-added H and C contracts of CG-B2-P7-023-2 are platform contracts of wave 0 and published contracts of rwb-case and of rwb-decision; they do not block the build and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which the plan gives as None and RWB-P3-E2012-CON. This story converges on them and builds against their published sets and fakes.
why: The metadata rows and the DP table of R5.5 must both hold; the DP table adds dependencies the plan slice does not list.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5; the story metadata rows; the fragment H and C lists
confirm: Delivery lead at the wave 2 dependency review
impact: If a DP-added contract slips, only the affected client or library waits; the record acceptance, the version in force and the two reads keep their own order and Day 1 stays

text: The record of a move is consumed once, as rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, and this story does not build a second consumer, a second hash chain, a second append-only trigger or a second Schedule: the ingest, the chain, the daily seal and the JOB-14 chain check at 02:00 are RWB-P7-E1008-APP's and are reused, and this story adds only the transfer-specific acceptance, the version in force and the two reads. The other form of the name, rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1, is recorded as the RWB-P7-E2027-APP value and must be dropped or filtered before the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog freeze.
why: Two consumers on one topic and two names for one event would seal one record twice or leave it unsealed, and two chains cannot both be the ledger.
read: RWB P7 E1008 APP sections 1, 12.4 and 12.6; RWB P7 E2027 APP section 12.3; RWB P3 E2012 APP section 12.3; TSD P7 v2 T5.3; Template and Rules v1 DP-09, DP-14
confirm: P7 solution architect with the event platform owner, before the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog freeze
impact: If the other event name wins, only the topic filter, the envelope assertion and AC2 change; the entry, its chain and the reads do not

text: No approval level of the delegation of authority applies to a manual transfer or reassignment, because a move changes work and not money; the record is therefore not an approval item, the approval table of rwb-decision is not used by this story, and ApprovalRequested is never raised for a transfer. The rights are those of legacy section 10: RW-TEAMMGR and RW-CAPACITY move, RW-CASEOWN and RW-AUDIT read.
why: The legacy story states it and the target must not turn a work item into a credit decision by accident.
read: Legacy sections 10 and 12; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (approval), T6.1 and T5.3; Template and Rules v1 R3
confirm: P7 business analyst at the wave 2 walkthrough
impact: If an approval were required, an approval row and an ApprovalRequested event would be added and the entry would name the approver; no version, rule or reason code changes

text: The TRANSFER package row and its version rows are single rows in rwb_decision: TRF-2026.12 in force from 2026-12-01 with TRF-2026.11 in force before it, as the legacy story and FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-007-05 give them. The rows are written by the registry stories RWB-P7-E1021-APP and RWB-P7-E1073-APP; where they have not landed, this story's seed registers the same two labels and the same dates once, and no second row for the same label is ever created.
why: The fill order of R7.3 puts the legacy story first for this story's values, and two rows for one label would put two versions in force on one date.
read: RWB E2 012 v2 sections 3, 7 and 8; FSD P7 v3 A2.7 AC-EXC-P7-007-05; RWB P7 E1021 APP; RWB P7 E1073 APP; Template and Rules v1 R7.3
confirm: Rule owner RW-COE with the P7 solution architect, before the first joint environment
impact: If the registry stories use other labels or dates, only the seed, AC6, AC7 and the version list answer change; the entry, its chain and the reads do not
